bib.title: Attention Is All You Need
bib.venue: 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017)

read.skipped: Reference list (offsets ~30200-36000) skimmed for lineage only; appendix attention-visualisation figures 3-5 contain only token text, no results.

question: Can a sequence transduction model built only on attention, with no recurrence or convolution, match or beat recurrent and convolutional encoder-decoders in translation quality while training faster?
hypothesis: Self-attention gives constant path length and full parallelism, so it should train faster and learn long-range dependencies more easily than RNNs or CNNs (stated as three desiderata in section 4).
contributions: The Transformer: the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention, with no sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution
Scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention
New WMT 2014 EN-DE and EN-FR results at a fraction of the training cost

method.summary: An encoder-decoder of 6+6 stacked layers, each built from multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network, with residual connections and layer norm. Input and output tokens are learned embeddings plus sinusoidal positional encodings; embedding and pre-softmax weights are shared. Trained on WMT 2014 translation, then applied to WSJ constituency parsing.
method.task: machine translation (WMT 2014 EN-DE, EN-FR) and English constituency parsing

datasets.name: WMT 2014 English-German
datasets.preprocessing: byte-pair encoding, shared source-target vocabulary of about 37000 tokens; batched by approximate length, about 25000 source and 25000 target tokens per batch

models.name: Transformer (base)
models.architecture: encoder-decoder transformer, post-norm, sinusoidal positions, tied embeddings

other.note: other parameters unchanged from EN-DE base model

training.objective: cross-entropy with label smoothing 0.1 (implied by label smoothing and perplexity; loss not named)
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then inverse square root decay
training.regularisation: residual dropout on sub-layer outputs and on embedding+positional sums; label smoothing 0.1
training.hardware: one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs

inference.decoding: beam search, beam size 4, length penalty alpha=0.6 (translation); beam 21, alpha=0.3 (parsing)

metrics.name: training cost
metrics.definition: training time x number of GPUs x sustained single-precision capacity per GPU (2.8, 3.7, 6.0, 9.5 TFLOPS for K80, K40, M40, P100)

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: per-wordpiece on dev, not comparable to per-word

eval.protocol: single run per configuration reported; no seeds, variance or significance test stated

evidence.quote: We trained our models on one machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.
consisting of about 4.5 million sentence pairs
We used beam search with a beam size of 4 and length penalty

results.claim: The big Transformer set a new EN-DE state of the art, more than 2 BLEU above prior models including ensembles.
results.setup: WMT 2014 EN-DE newstest2014, big model, 3.5 days on 8 P100, last 20 checkpoints averaged, beam 4; baseline is ConvS2S Ensemble
results.quote: establishing a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4

results.claim: On EN-FR the big model is a new single-model best, but the paper prints 41.8 in the abstract and Table 2 and 41.0 in section 6.1.
results.setup: WMT 2014 EN-FR newstest2014, big model with dropout 0.1; baseline is best single model (MoE); ConvS2S ensemble reaches 41.29
results.quote: our big model achieves a BLEU score of 41.0

results.claim: The base model already beats all prior EN-DE models and ensembles at 3.3e18 FLOPs, but scores 38.1 on EN-FR, below earlier single models.
results.setup: WMT 2014 newstest2014, base model, 100K steps / 12 h; FLOPs are an estimate
results.quote: Even our base model surpasses all previously published models and ensembles, at a fraction of the training cost of any of the competitive models.

results.claim: EN-FR big model reached its score at under a quarter of the training cost of the previous state of the art.
results.quote: at less than 1/4 the training cost of the previous state-of-the-art model

results.claim: Learned positional embeddings give nearly identical results to sinusoids.
results.setup: EN-DE newstest2013 dev, base model, no checkpoint averaging; row (E) learned vs base sinusoidal
results.quote: observe nearly identical results to the base model

results.claim: A single attention head is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting, and too many heads also hurts.
results.setup: EN-DE newstest2013 dev, constant computation, rows (A)
results.quote: single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting, quality also drops off with too many heads

results.claim: Reducing key size d_k hurts quality; bigger models and dropout help.
results.quote: reducing the attention key size dk hurts model quality

results.claim: A 4-layer Transformer reaches 91.3 F1 on WSJ-only parsing and 92.7 semi-supervised, with little task-specific tuning.
results.setup: WSJ Section 23, semi-supervised with about 17M sentences; baselines McClosky 2006 / Vinyals & Kaiser 2014; WSJ-only score is 91.3

results.claim: Self-attention layer cost is O(n^2 d) with O(1) sequential ops and O(1) path length, against O(n) for recurrent layers.
results.setup: Table 1; self-attention is cheaper than recurrence when n < d
results.quote: self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence

results.claim: Dividing dot products by sqrt(d_k) is needed because their variance grows with d_k and pushes softmax into tiny-gradient regions.
results.setup: argument with footnote assuming q,k components independent, mean 0, variance 1; not an ablation

limits: Evidence is two translation tasks and one parsing task; no claim about language modelling or other modalities, which the authors list as future work.
Single reported run per configuration; no seeds or significance tests.
The paper gives 41.8 and 41.0 for the EN-FR big model; the two are not reconciled.
FLOPs are estimates from GPU time and nominal capacity, not measured.
Perplexities are per-wordpiece and not comparable to per-word numbers.
Attention-as-interpretability is shown only by hand-picked examples (Figs 3-5).
Authors name restricted/local attention for long inputs and less sequential generation as open work.
Dated: post-norm LayerNorm, ReLU FFN, sinusoidal positions and 6-layer scale are not the current default; the note's use should be as origin, not recipe.
